notes: PHASE-000 foundation is complete and PHASE-001 development is active. WU-002 remains in progress because its acceptance criterion is not yet satisfied: approved desktop calling applications have not consumed processed/bypass audio through an installed OS-visible VSN virtual microphone. The verified Windows foundation includes Rust audio contracts and bounded queues, deterministic device selection/reselection, bounded stream recovery, IAudioClient3 planning, event-driven WASAPI capture, sample decode/reframing, CaptureRuntime reopen recovery, IMMNotificationClient delivery, bounded virtual-mic staging/output, a versioned Rust protocol, MSVC x64 C++ ABI mirror, aligned Interlocked cursor publication, deterministic shared-region geometry and real user-mode section mapping. The original user-supplied-section CONNECT assumption was replaced by a driver-owned section handshake in merge 3953069f468c46d744f30625b3696e5b12f03a77 after AI Native run 34537871677 and Windows run 34537871806 passed. CONNECT v2 carries validated protocol geometry rather than a caller-provided section handle; the driver is responsible for creating the section and returning a user handle only after initialization. The subsequent KMDF control-driver slice adds an official-WDK-buildable x64 Desktop driver project using pinned Microsoft WDK/SDK NuGet 10.0.28000.2526, a SYSTEM/Administrators-only development device interface, METHOD_BUFFERED CONNECT/DISCONNECT/QUERY_STATUS dispatch, requestor process/file ownership checks, driver-created paging-file section creation in the requestor process context, an independently retained section-object reference, system-space mapping, protocol/cursor initialization, QUERY_STATUS cursor reads and bounded release on disconnect, file cleanup and device cleanup. AI Native Quality Gates run 34539554036 and Windows Audio Validation run 34539554115 both passed on implementation head 6bb193f96ecec505f341600b5577b18e4046a89c; the Windows run restored the pinned WDK packages, built vsn_virtual_mic_control.sys successfully with WDK validation enabled, and then passed the existing C++ transport-contract executables. The slice merged to main as b2761ad400d92c1d810751fabcf4b071a40dfb9c. This proves a WDK-buildable KMDF control plane and secure driver-owned shared-section lifecycle, not an audio miniport or OS-visible microphone. Still pending are a WaveRT/PortCls capture endpoint and topology, kernel ring-consumer timing/position behavior tied to the retained shared region, INF/package installation and test-signing on a controlled Windows machine, endpoint enumeration and runtime DeviceIoControl evidence, least-privilege non-admin broker/interface policy, processed/bypass audio reaching approved calling applications, physical-device recovery evidence, hardware CPU/latency/jitter/deadline measurements, and production signing/update/uninstall/rollback verification. The next valid WU-002 action is to establish the minimal WDK WaveRT/PortCls virtual-microphone endpoint/topology and kernel-side ring-consumer path against the verified control/shared-region contracts, then add controlled-machine install/enumeration/runtime evidence before any OS-visible endpoint or calling-app compatibility claim. Paid provider usage, proprietary model training, production credentials/cloud spend and production deployment remain subject to applicable provider/data/compute/release gates.
